We're looking for a motivated working student to help turn these questions into experiments and experiments into maintainable code. You'll explore optimization methods and build reusable evaluation tooling. You'll work closely with our quantization, compiler, and runtime engineers, and your findings will directly influence how we optimize models for Tensordyne hardware. What you will do Model quality evaluation: Measure how low-precision computation affects performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks. Diagnose where quantization has the greatest impact. Quantization research: Implement and compare post-training quantization methods to improve inference efficiency while preserving task accuracy. Build reproducible tooling: Automate evaluations, track configurations and results, and make experiments accessible to engineers and AI agents. Measure runtime performance: Characterize latency, throughput, and memory usage to understand bottlenecks under different deployment scenarios. A first project could involve exploring the quality–performance Pareto frontier of a Qwen or LlaMa model. You'll experiment with 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantization configurations to find the best runtime-quality tradeoff. Core qualifications Current enrollment in Computer Science, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related master's degree program. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, including the ability to understand and modify model implementations. Effective use of AI coding tools and critical review of their output. An experimental mindset: you can formulate hypotheses, design comparisons, and draw careful conclusions from noisy results. Clear communication and the ability to present experimental findings and technical tradeoffs to the team. Strong pluses: experience with quantization, LLM evaluation, performance profiling, or inference optimization. This role is for you if you thrive on responsibility, learn quickly, and are naturally proactive . What we offer Join a deep-tech team building the next generation of AI inference systems. Put your university knowledge into practice with leading open-source LLMs, deepen your understanding of quantization and inference optimization, and build skills in experimental design, software engineering, and AI coding tools. You'll own a focused project, receive close mentorship from experienced engineers, and have room to explore ideas that shape our optimization methods. title: Lead .NET Engineer
description: Location : Onsite, full time at our Buyerlink office right on the Inner Harbour of Victoria, BC! Working hours: Standard full-time business hours, with an early overlap window with our Armenia team About the role We operate a marketplace that connects car shoppers with dealers and manufacturers. The systems behind it run on .NET, they are customer facing, and they carry live transaction volume every hour of the day. When something goes wrong, dealers notice, consumers notice, and revenue moves. That is the level of consequence this role sits at. This is the platform ownership role. You will set the technical direction for the marketplace platform, make the architecture calls, and be the person accountable for its health. Two engineers cover it, you in North America and a senior engineer in Armenia. That is a deliberate design: an eleven hour offset means the marketplace has senior engineering attention through the working day on both sides of the world, which matters for a system our customers use around the clock. What gets built, in what order, and what moves overnight is yours to decide. This is not a role where you take tickets off a queue. You will be one of a small number of people who understand these systems deeply, and you will be expected to act like it. How the role is structured You will report to our VP of Engineering and work daily with engineering, product, and business colleagues across the United States, Latin America, Armenia, and Ukraine. Our US stakeholders will come to you directly, and translating what they need into technical work is a real part of the job. You will lead the senior .NET engineer in Armenia on this platform. You set their technical direction, decide what they pick up, and review what comes back. To be precise about the boundary, this is technical leadership rather than people management. Their employment relationship sits with our Armenia organization, so hiring, performance, and compensation are not yours. Everything about how the platform gets built is. The practical shape of it is a handoff twice a day. What you leave behind at the end of yours determines how their day goes, and the reverse. Leads who write things down and give context in advance get real leverage out of the offset. Leads who keep the important context in their heads do not. One thing to be clear about: as the platform owner in this hemisphere, production issues that surface outside the Armenia working day come to you. What you will do Own the design, development, testing, and release of features across customer-facing .NET applications and the services behind them. Take production issues from first report to resolved root cause, including the ones that surface during your hours and need a decision now rather than after a meeting. Modernize as you go. Parts of this platform predate current .NET, and moving them forward without interrupting a live marketplace is a core part of the job rather than a side project. Design and build APIs that partners, dealers, and internal systems depend on. Work on SQL Server performance and data design, including query and schema work on systems under real load. Direct the work of the senior engineer in Armenia: set priorities, scope what they take on overnight, review what comes back, and give them enough context to make good calls without you. Build a handoff practice that actually works, so overnight coverage produces progress rather than a queue of questions. Review code and raise the standard of what ships. Translate business requirements from product and marketing partners into technical designs, and push back when the requirement and the system are pointing in different directions. Working with AI Every developer here has Claude and GitHub Copilot, and they are part of how the work gets done rather than an optional extra. What matters to us is judgment: knowing which tasks to hand to a model and which to write yourself, giving it enough context to return something usable, and reviewing what comes back as carefully as you would review any other engineer's pull request. You should be able to explain every line you merge. The more important thing to know is where this is heading. Over the next six to twelve months we expect to move substantially toward agentic development, with agents taking on larger and more autonomous portions of the build and test cycle. That will change our tooling, our workflow, and what the day-to-day job looks like. We are not asking you to have done this before, because very few people have. We are asking you to be genuinely interested in figuring it out with us, and comfortable working in an environment where the way we build is still being reshaped. If you would rather join a team with a settled toolchain, this is an honest reason to look elsewhere. If that prospect is the interesting part, we should talk. What you bring 5 to 8 years building and supporting production .NET applications, including time as the senior person others came to. Strong C# and ASP.NET, across both modern .NET and the older framework versions that real businesses still run on. API design and development experience, including integrations that external partners depend on. Real SQL Server depth: query optimization, indexing, and schema design against systems under load. Production experience on Azure. Our platform runs there. Enough front-end familiarity (JavaScript, HTML, CSS) to work effectively on customer-facing applications. Judgment about legacy code. Knowing when to modernize, when to leave it alone, and how to tell the difference. Experience directing other engineers' work, formally or not. You should be able to describe a time you set someone else's technical direction and what you did when it went sideways. Comfort working through change. Our stack and our development practices are actively evolving, and you should find that energizing rather than unsettling. Clear written communication. A distributed team with overnight handoffs runs on writing. Nice to have Experience in automotive, marketplaces, lead generation, or another high-volume transactional domain. Migration experience, particularly legacy .NET Framework to modern .NET, or on-premises SQL Server to Azure SQL. Multi-threading and parallel processing work. Familiarity with XML and XSLT, which appear in parts of this platform. CI/CD and automated testing practice. Agile delivery in a distributed team. Why work with us The systems here matter and the team is small enough that you will see the effect of your work directly. We invest ahead of the curve on tooling, we retire what no longer serves us, and we would rather ship and learn than deliberate indefinitely. If you want scope rather than a slice of someone else's plan, there is plenty of it. Compensation Salary Range: $110, 000 - $130, 000 CAD Compensation will be determined by factors including knowledge and skills, role-specific qualifications, market location, and experience.
